definitions.explanation: The number ten thousand. A key unit in Japanese counting, as large numbers are grouped by 万 (ten thousands) rather than thousands.

examples.japanese: {百万|ひゃくまん}{円|えん}の{車|くるま}を{買|か}いました。
examples.english: I bought a car for 1,000,000 yen.

examples.japanese: {東京|とうきょう}には{一千万人|いっせんまんにん}{以上|いじょう}が{住|す}んでいます。
examples.english: More than 10 million people live in Tokyo.

examples.japanese: {三万|さんまん}{円|えん}{貸|か}してくれませんか。
この{店|みせ}では{五万|ごまん}{円|えん}{以上|いじょう}{買|か}うと{送料|そうりょう}が{無料|むりょう}です。
examples.english: At this store, shipping is free if you buy 50,000 yen or more.

notes:
{万|まん} (ten thousand) is a fundamental unit in the Japanese number system. Large numbers are grouped by {万|まん}, not by thousands as in English.

COUNTING SYSTEM:
- {一万|いちまん}: 10,000
- {十万|じゅうまん}: 100,000
- {百万|ひゃくまん}: 1,000,000
- {千万|せんまん}: 10,000,000
- {一億|いちおく}: 100,000,000 (next unit)

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {万一|まんいち}: by any chance, in case of emergency
- {万全|ばんぜん}: perfect, complete
- {万歳|ばんざい}: banzai, long live

CURRENCY NOTE:
{一万円|いちまんえん}{札|さつ} is the 10,000-yen bill, the largest denomination in Japan.

TIP FOR LEARNERS:
When converting, remember: 1 million = 100{万|まん}, not 1000{万|まん}.
